open_items.text: Bind the E_DoorState and E_LockState enumerators. The game ships Unreal's unrenamed NewEnumeratorN defaults, so the meaning is not in the bytes. Method: watch one door on screen while polling the save, and read which enumerator changes - the same wall-clock join that bound the class ids. Observed so far: DoorState 1/2/3, LockState 0/2, with DoorState 0 and LockState 1 never seen in 22,973 values

The three-integer map key is measured positional (per-axis correlation +0.992/+0.941/+0.969 against Translation on the 22 dead monsters, key/100 within 102 to 1,524 units). WHICH frame it encodes - placement, spawn, or position at first save - and the physical unit of either quantity are unmeasured. DoorData and TreasureBoxMap carry no Transform, so the confirmation available is monsters-only. Watching one actor across two runs to see whether its key is stable would separate the readings

PlayzoneData is a shrinking-circle mechanic (DmgCircle and SafeCircle, each a Vector2D centre plus a radius, plus FinialSafeCircleLocation and ElapseTime). In this capture the damage and safe circles are identical to the bit, so the zone had not started moving. Whether they ever diverge, and whether the talent Gyldenmist Tolerance names this mechanic, are both UNMEASURED - do not write the talent binding down until something observed connects them
